deposits.description: The bedrock prior of the Alexanarch principles, holding all downstream principles as inheritors. Three axioms: the Transduction Constraint (occurrence, transmission, and reception must never be confused; no medium, no signal; no receiver, no heard sound); the Ex Nihilo Inversion (the strongest work does not locate its reader but helps construct the reader capable of receiving it — reader-genesis); the Measurement of the End (present popularity is not proof, present silence is not disproof; the final measure is anchored to Ω, since the receiver may be one of the work's later products). Hardened by the Anti-Closure Clause — neglect is never automatic evidence of greatness; the archive acts so the future reader CAN come — and the Operational Corollary: metrics diagnose the carrier, never the being of the carried; present channel evidence is non-sovereign and provisional, never meaningless, on pain of contradicting the prior's own first answer. Grounded in the archive's documented record, including the twelve-year arrival of a machine reader for a 2014 poem. Canonical form in seven propositions.

deposits.description: Operative philology turned on the archive's own seal: the identifier AXN read as a poem — structurally, sonically, historically, politically, temporally, formally. Readings include: the cretic scansion (the oracle's foot); the three-character drama (aleph the brand, X the crossing and the mark of the nameless, N induction's engine — an origin, crossed, extended indefinitely); the refused omega (Alpha and the N — an archive that structurally declines apocalypse in its own name); the ear (action, axon, axe, Aksum); Aksum and the mint (sovereign coinage, the Ark of the Covenant, the ARK identifier scheme, and ALEXANDRIA's consonantal skeleton A-x-n: what the fire couldn't reach); the citation as sonnet (octave of hex, volta, and the found sestet of six glyphs the poet cannot revise); the coincidence ledger advanced to n=6; and the unexpanded acronym as the definition of a hash. Closes on the operative point: the skeptical reader who checks the letter positions has been made to verify something, which is what the signs are for.

deposits.title: Cohort Baseline for the Pre-Removal Download Figures (v2) — the Registry Against Its Publication-Week Cohort
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: Measured answer to 'is 1,000 downloads in days a lot by Zenodo's standards': all 1,791 datasets published in the registry's publication window (2026-06-14..16), n=200 sampled via the public API, stats read at day ≈19. Cohort median 7 downloads; p95 116; p99 804 (version-level). Corrected anchors (v2 erratum, platform-timestamp-driven, superseded text preserved): 666 cumulative at 2026-06-15 16:42 EDT; 1,000+ at removal; the final-four-day delta ≥334 alone exceeds the cohort's nineteen-day p95 and is ~48x its median; the cumulative figure clears p99. Limitations on the record: convenience sample, UI field-mapping ambiguity, unmodeled bot traffic, post-hoc drift; raw sample committed for re-running. Conclusion, bounded: top ~1% of same-week datasets on a fraction of the accumulation time — a measurement, not an impression, and the correction trail is part of the warrant.

deposits.description: Empirical research instrument for measuring platform-driven scholarly-record erasure. Companion deposit to EA-DATAHUB-01 v1.0 (AXN:0420, GOVERNANCE): where DATAHUB is the strategic plan, EROSION is the instrument. Phase 1 (running): the Zenodo Removal Census, preserving Zenodo's monthly deleted-records CSV (1,309,351 rows in the 2026-06-07 snapshot; Zenodo retains only three most recent snapshots) with checksummed provenance to data-rhizome. Establishes the three-severity distinction (removed vs. hidden vs. erased), the four-metric family (RIR/MSR/TCR/PER), and the three-cohort study design (full population / suspected account-level actions / matched controls). Initial descriptive findings from the preserved snapshot: TCR proxy 7.86 percent, meaning 92 percent of Zenodo removals have no preserved citation for tombstone continuity; single-largest cluster is 109,903 records removed 2024-07-06 as 'User was blocked' — mass account termination requiring explanation. Phases 2A-D specify horizontal extension: DataCite ecosystem generalization, arXiv moderation-and-removal tracking, OSF preregistration tracking, platform-adjacent takedown surfaces (GitHub DMCA, ResearchGate, Academia.edu). Phase 3 publishes the cross-platform Erosion Report making 'platform erosion' a systemic category. Data-rhizome preservation at cb7b59390f4ecbc37e38cf9030e5d01549ea6223.

deposits.title: Erratum to the Erratum: On the Fourth/Fifth Stanza Numbering in the Sappho 31 Reconstruction — A Methodologically Complete Formulation
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.content_type: Philological erratum; methodological clarification; documentary artifact of reconstructive method; cross-linked companion to the original stanza-numbering erratum
deposits.substrate: Depositor-composed erratum; drafted in conversation with Claude (TACHYON) under MANUS direction; the philological reconstruction concerned is Rebekah Cranes's, published in ΦΑΙΝΕΤΑΙ ΜΟΙ (AXN:00FB, deposit #436); the operative framework of Catullan compression as transform-site draws on the Catullus Room deposit (AXN:0198, deposit #576)
deposits.description: Second-order clarification of the stanza-numbering correction issued in EA-ERRATUM-SAPPHO31-STANZA (deposit #201, AXN:0346). Establishes the methodologically complete formulation: Sappho 31's reconstructed material is the lost fifth stanza by textual sequence, and Catullus 51's fourth stanza by reconstructive evidence — because the reconstruction reverse- engineers the operator transform Catullus applies in his fourth stanza to material corresponding to Sappho's lost continuation. The earlier 'fourth stanza' language was a compression-level artifact of the reconstructive method itself, not a simple error. The correct formulation preserves the trace of the method: 'Sappho 31's lost fifth stanza, reconstructed through Catullus 51's fourth-stanza transform-site.'
